title: Pipeline node
description: A hypothesised APPROACH to a goal — the 'how-we're-trying' layer (ADR-0005). Distinct from a goal_node (the 'why'): densify, joint-grid-pivot, cross-cloud, single-wind-window-polish are METHODS, not questions, and were mis-filed as goal_nodes. A Pipeline is the hub the lateral edges attach to: it `serves` >=1 Goal, `composes` Tools (substrate_components), and may `supersede` a rival Pipeline. Experiments attach to it via run_record.tests (Experiment -> tests -> Pipeline); the reverse (tested_by) is derived, not stored. Stored one-file-per-node under research_os/pipelines/, git-friendly like goal_nodes.

id.description: pipeline_<kebab-slug>. Stable; runs reference it via tests[], rivals via supersedes/superseded_by.

hypothesis.description: What this approach BETS on — the one-line wager that distinguishes it from a rival pipeline (e.g. 'densifying the ω-grid closes anchor starvation without oracle').

state.description: open = under exploration. blocked = waiting on a dependency. closed = explored to a verdict (success or dead). revivable = closed but its blocker may no longer hold. superseded = a rival pipeline replaced it (superseded_by must be set).

serves.description: goal_node ids this pipeline is an approach to (Pipeline -> serves -> Goal). >=1; a method can serve more than one goal (that is exactly the reuse signal a tree can't show).

composes.description: substrate_component ids this pipeline is built from (Pipeline -> composes -> Tool). A Tool composed by many pipelines is a transfer/reuse hub. When `steps` is present this SHOULD equal the set of step tools (the flat reuse-hub view of the runnable DAG).

steps.description: The runnable DAG (ADR-0007 §5.3). Ordered steps; each runs ONE Tool via the executor (loop/run_pipeline.py) and feeds the next. OPTIONAL — a pipeline with no `steps` is descriptive-only (its `composes` set still documents the Tools it draws on). Listed order MUST be a valid topological order: a step may reference only earlier steps (or pipeline inputs). The two combinators ADR-0007 §2 names: `compose` (invoke once, chain) and `map` (lift a per-epoch Tool across a collection -> a set of outputs).

id.description: Step name, unique within the pipeline. Later steps reference its output via the ref `$steps.<id>` (or `$steps.<id>.<key>`).

op.description: compose = invoke the Tool once. map = lift the per-epoch Tool across `over` (a collection), producing a LIST of outputs ('a cloud for the whole LC is the same Tool mapped over a window', ADR-0007 §2).

tool.description: substrate_component id this step runs. Referential: must resolve to a Tool. The drift-check (tool_lint) runs on it before invocation, exactly as the run-button does.

params.description: Param overrides for THIS step, layered over the Tool's default_params (ADR-0007 'variation lives in params, not copies').

inputs.description: Wire the Tool's kwargs from the run context. A string VALUE beginning with `$` is a REF: `$in.<key>` (a pipeline input) or `$steps.<step_id>[.<key>]` (a prior step's whole output, or one key of its dict). Any other value is a literal. A kwarg not wired here falls back to params / the Tool's own default.

over.description: map only: a ref (`$in.*` / `$steps.*`) to the collection each invocation iterates. Per element, the element binds to the kwarg named by `map_as`. Ignored when op=compose.

map_as.description: map only: the Tool kwarg each element of `over` binds to (e.g. `epoch`). Null = if the element is a dict, spread it as kwargs.

supersedes.description: pipeline id this one replaces (Pipeline -> supersedes -> Pipeline, rivalry/supersession). The replaced pipeline carries the mirror superseded_by + state=superseded.

superseded_by.description: pipeline id that replaced this one. Set <=> state == superseded.

last_measured.description: The most recent headline result a run produced on this approach.

run.description: run_record id of the measuring run.
